questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The University of Edinburgh is ranked as one of the best universities in the UK and the world and therefore was a perfect choice for an academic challenge because of its well-known reputation. Further, I've talked to former exchange students who recommended the university because of its way of welcoming exchange students. The university is known for hosting many international students so there is plenty of opportunity to make international connections. Last, I wanted to explore Scottish nature and culture (which didn't disappoint).

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My study abroad experience was overall good. However, some of my courses did not live up to my expectations.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was pretty easy but the University of Edinburgh has a tendency to send an overwhelming amount of emails which inflict more harm than good.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I received emails concerning my arrival and what to remember. Further, I was assigned a personal student advisor.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Sometimes an overwhelming amount of information from the university.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer:
Most international students were offered accommodation through the university, so it was quite easy to find.

As for recommendations, I think it is pretty difficult to find private housing since the housing market is booming. Therefore, you must be out early and look for rooms/apartments, and actively search Facebook groups and webpages. I would also recommend joining exchange whatsapp groups from the former semester since people often write in these in the end looking for tenants for the coming semester.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: I think it is easier to live near campus since it is often closer to the city centre. However, if you don't mind public transport (which is free for people under 22) or walking, it should be fine.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: My university housing was like a dorm room in Copenhagen. I had my own bath and bedroom but shared a kitchen with my five roommates. My accommodation was more modern compared to other university housing, so overall it was good. However, it was a bit far away from my classes.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I had to fill out an online application. The process was fairly easy but slow.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I could always write an email to the university if I needed help.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I was not successful since I only got one of the courses I wanted. However, I did change my preferences 1 1/2 months after my original registration, hence the new courses I wanted were already full. It was therefore my own fault.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be sure of which courses you want and apply for them as soon as possible. There is limited space in most year 2 and 3 courses of around 30 people, so the courses fill out quickly.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The low score is mostly related to the fact I wasn't enrolled in my preferred courses.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: MA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The amount of obligatory reading was more than I expected in all the courses. However, the level was as I expected taking into account that some of my courses were year 3 (and therefore more demanding) and others year 1.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer:
The seminars are in some ways similar to UCPH. They consist of a class which then discusses the topic of the day. One of my year 3 courses called Gifts in Context was mostly taught through an abstract debate of the obligatory reading, so it was pretty difficult to follow the topic sometimes. It was rare you came out with any answers since it was more about reflection and discussion. 
Moreover, both my year 3 courses did not use any PowerPoint at all, which we usually do at UCPH

Further, the structure of the lectures is also similar to UCHP's lectures. However, my lectures were only online but that was a decision of the course organisation for that specific course. One also has to be aware that if the course is a year 1 course, it is mostly lectures and a few tutorials (similar to seminars) where you discuss the lecture in more depth.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to global crime and justice (year 1)
Contemporary Issues in Competition Law and the Single Market (year 3)
Gifts in Context (year 3)

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I really enjoyed Contemporary Issues in Competition Law and the Single Market since it is also usable in Denmark because of the EU rules.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: I did not encounter any unexpected cost.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: In general, Scotland is around 10% cheaper compared to the prices in Denmark. Therefore, grocery shopping, eating out, etc. was less expensive than I expected.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Edinburgh University offers plenty of non-academic opportunities.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The university offers a range of cultural/social societies. For example, the university has a harry potter society, a whisky society, an anime and animations society, a bad film society, the Erasmus society etc. Besides the societies, the university also has plenty of sports clubs + a gym for university staff and students.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I would recommend joining the Erasmus Society since they arrange trips to other parts of Scotland. This is a great way to explore Scotland since you just have to show up and enjoy the trip. Moreover, it is a great way to meet other exchange students.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: As described above, I would recommend buying Erasmus trips. They offer both day trips and 2 to 3 days trips. By doing that, you are sure to see the most popular spots in Scotland such as the Highlands. Further, I would recommend arranging your own day trips to Scottish cities such as Glasgow, Aberdeen, and so on. You can also take the train and bus to multiple cities in the two national parks, so I would recommend exploring the parks and going on some hiking trips.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: It was very easy since the culture is similar to the culture Copenhagen.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: I would join a society or a sports club since it otherwise can be hard to socialize with local students.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: There as not particularly challenging differences.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer:
I especially enjoyed the pub culture in Scotland since almost all pubs offer both a meal and drinks. I have enjoyed many beers with my friends at different pubs during my exchange. I also appreciated how friendly and helpful the Scottish people in general are.

I also appreciated the fact that most museums were free so it was easy to explore the cities on a low budget. 

A little tip is also that tap water is free, so always ask for tap water at restaurants, cafes, and so on.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
1. Remember to explore outside the city. Scotland has amazing nature!
2. Try out the local pub culture and some pub quizzes. 
3. Don't be afraid to challenge yourself. Go to events where you don't know anyone - maybe you'll find a new friend.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Consider making a list of activities and trips you want to do before you arrive. Time goes by fast, and before you know it, the semester is over. By making a list, you are sure to have an overview of everything you want to explore.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Definitely getting to know all the wonderful international people. It was amazing learning about different cultures and also developing friendships with people from all around the world.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: There were not any specific challenging circumstances, but overall moving to another country without knowing anyone can be challenging and difficult - but also very rewarding if you hang in there.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
